answer: Neighborhood Bridge Control.** Each identity registers one bridge edge to an existing node, and routing credits flow only along edges where both endpoints maintain distinct neighbor sets. An identity whose neighbors overlap heavily with its own registrant's neighbors gets throttled, since farms produce dense local clusters. To sustain Sybil throughput, an attacker must grow an orchard of mutually distant connections, paying real latency and routing costs per extra edge.
